newsitem.title: USA: BP says halts work on Alaska Northstar lease.
newsitem.headline: BP says halts work on Alaska Northstar lease.

text.p: BP Exploration Alaska Inc said Thursday it would suspend construction of offshore production facilities at its Northstar oil prospect in Alaska until a lawsuit challenging the lease's legality is resolved.
The lawsuit, filed against the State of Alaska by a former legislative candidate, claimed new royalty concessions on the lease are illegal, the company said.
"The fabrication work on the project is being suspended...pending resolution of the lawsuit," said BP Exploration spokesman Paul Laird.

BP has spent $50 million so far on development of the lease, which it acquired from Amerada Hess Corp and Shell Oil in early 1995, Laird said. The field has recoverable reserves of about 145 million barrels and is expected to come on line in 1999.
BP planned to begin construction of processing facilities and staff housing in the coming weeks, he added.
The company had budgeted over $400 million for Northstar's development, but the delay will add unknown costs.
"We don't have a timeline for when the case will be resolved," Laird said.

The suspension of Northstar's development will affect the phasing in of the company's five-year, $3.5 billion Alaskan capital expenditure plan, but the total budget remains intact, BP said in a statement.
